note: The penstemons, coneflowers, Culver's roots and spurges of 0.9.162, and boneset, which is where 'Milk and Cookies' belongs: it is Eupatorium perfoliatum, not a Euphorbia. Every penstemon, Echinacea, Veronicastrum and spurge here was redrawn; the records below are the ones added or resized. Sizes are MBG Plant Finder figures unless an estimate says otherwise; heightIn is the plant in flower, near the middle of MBG's range.

sources.mbg: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, https://plantfinder.mobot.org/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=<id>, read 2026-11-24

penstemon|pocahontas.estimates: MBG 3-4 ft x 2-3 ft, lavender pink. Bred from a dark-leaved selection; MBG's text does not say the cultivar's own leaves are dark, so they are drawn green.

penstemon|onyxandpearls.estimates: MBG 3-3.5 ft x 3-3.5 ft, pale purple to nearly white flowers, a dark-leaved selection.

penstemon|blackbeard.estimates: MBG 2.5-3 ft; dark purple leaves and stems, pink flowers.

beardlippenstemon.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft x 1-1.5 ft, rose red, May-June; rocky slopes from Utah and Colorado to Arizona, Texas and Mexico. Its basal leaves keep some green in winter, but no Winter foliage is authored: a green Winter leaf would skip the spring cutback and stand the flower stems all year.

cobaeapenstemon.estimates: MBG 1-2 ft (its text says 1-2.5 ft), white, pink to violet, May; 2 in flowers. Prairies and limestone glades of the Great Plains and Ozarks.

foothillpenstemon|electricblue.estimates: MBG 1-1.5 ft x 1-1.5 ft, gentian blue.

rockymountainpenstemon.estimates: Existing record's figures kept; joined the Penstemon card.

echinacea|rubystar.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft x 2-3 ft, carmine red to purple rays, bronze-brown cone. 'Rubinstern' is the cultivar name, Ruby Star its trade name.

echinacea|fragrantangel.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft, white rays, yellow-orange cone.

echinacea|sombrerosalsared.estimates: MBG 1.5-2 ft, orange-red rays, orange-brown cone. 'Balsomsed' is the cultivar name.

echinacea|greenenvy.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft, light green and pink bicolour; drawn as green rays flushed magenta from the cone outward.

echinacea|harvestmoon.estimates: MBG 2-2.5 ft, golden yellow rays, orange cone. 'Matthew Saul', Big Sky series; MBG files it under Echinacea alone, a hybrid with no wild range.

echinacea|milkshake.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft, white double; Cone-fections series.

tennesseeconeflower.estimates: MBG 1.5-2 ft, rose-purple upturned rays, coppery-orange cone. MBG gives zones 5-6 for the species and 5-8 for 'Rocky Top'; 5-8 is used. Cedar glades of middle Tennessee.

tennesseeconeflower|rockytop.estimates: MBG 2-2.5 ft, pink rays, blackish cone.

culvers|album.estimates: MBG 3-4 ft, white with pink stamens.

siberianculvers.estimates: MBG 3-5 ft x 1-3 ft, lavender-lilac, July-September.

euphorbiawulfenii|tasmaniantiger.estimates: MBG 2-3 ft ('to 3 ft tall' in its text), variegated leaves, pale yellow and cream bracts; a chance seedling of 'Lambrook Gold' found in Hobart.

cushionspurge|bonfire.estimates: MBG 1-1.5 ft; leaves turn deep red, orange and purple in spring, burgundy by midsummer, rich red in fall. MBG files it under E. epithymoides, a synonym here.

martinispurge.estimates: MBG lists only cultivars of the cross: 'Ascot Rainbow' 1.5-3 ft, zones 6-9; 'Sahara Blackbird' 1-2 ft. 24 in from those. A natural hybrid of E. characias and E. amygdaloides found in southern France, so a wild range with hybrid provenance.

martinispurge|ascotrainbow.estimates: MBG 1.5-3 ft, green and yellow bracts; variegated leaves.

martinispurge|blackbird.estimates: MBG 1-2 ft; 'Nothowlee', sold as Sahara Blackbird, dark purple leaves.

sweetspurge.estimates: MBG 1-1.5 ft (its text says 9-20 in), dark green to bronze leaves, greenish-yellow bracts.

sweetspurge|chameleon.estimates: MBG: leaves emerge dusky purple, rich burgundy-purple by summer, deeper purple with red in fall.

floweringspurge.estimates: MBG has no page for the species; its 'Carolina Snow' page describes the species: 0.5-3 ft, spreading to 1.5-2 ft, white petal-like appendages, summer into early fall, prairies and glades of the eastern and central US. 24 in used.

floweringspurge|carolinasnow.estimates: MBG: a floriferous selection with a showy, long-lasting display; drawn with fuller sprays.

woodspurge.estimates: MBG 1.5-2 ft x 0.75-1.5 ft (its text says 12-20 in); evergreen, purple-tinted beneath, burgundy in cold weather, yellow-green bracts April-June.

woodspurge|rubyglow.estimates: MBG: bright ruby-red spring leaves maturing purple-black, cherry-red stems. 'Waleuphglo'.

mrsrobbsbonnet.estimates: Existing record's figures kept; joined the Wood Spurge card and the new heads, on the spike form.

boneset.estimates: MBG 4-6 ft x 3-4 ft, white, July-September, medium to wet soil.

boneset|milkandcookies.estimates: MBG 3-3.5 ft x 1-1.5 ft, white, July-August; maroon-red foliage.

left_out.Echinacea purpurea 'PowWow Wild Berry': Not in the MBG Plant Finder; no source read.
left_out.Euphorbia polychroma 'Candy': MBG gives its size but not what sets it apart; it would draw as the species.
left_out.Euphorbia x martini 'Tiny Tim': No description read beyond MBG's size line.
left_out.Euphorbia myrsinites and E. cyparissias: Weedy: MBG and several states flag them as invasive or noxious.
left_out.Penstemon hybrids ('Red Rocks', 'Prairie: Left for a later batch; the species and the digitalis selections came first.
